newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Welfare submits defence against closure.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Welfare submits defence against closure.

text.p: Turkey's Islam-based Welfare Party on Monday submitted its formal defence against a legal bid threatening it with closure, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.
It said Welfare Party lawyers handed in the written defence to the constitutional court on Monday afternoon, shortly before the passing of a deadline set two months ago.
The party, the largest in Turkey's 550-seat parliament, faces closure by the court for allegedly threatening Turkey's secular constitution.
The defence is expected to be examined by the court in sessions closed to the media.
Welfare leader Necmettin Erbakan resigned as prime minister in June after months of pressure from Turkey's secularist establishment led by the military.

His year-long coalition with the conservatives of Tansu Ciller caused deep alarm in the powerful military by launching a series of largely symbolic challenges to NATO member Turkey's secular and pro-Western traditions.
